why: The recorder must decorate `effectiveInput` -- what the driver is actually handed -- and not the raw input controller, or an autoplay session records an empty stream while a normal session looks perfect. RE-MEASURED after the couch co-op input-routing PR, which the PR's own plan flagged as load-bearing: `effectiveInput` now yields `InputState[]` (list-shaped, one entry per active slot) while `input` (slot 0's raw controller alone) still yields a bare `InputState`. This tool does not run tsc, so that type mismatch is not caught structurally -- at runtime the mutated recorder's `sample()` calls `encodeTick` on a bare `InputState`, which has no `.map`, and throws `TypeError: inputs.map is not a function` inside driver.ts's frame() the first time a simulating frame samples input with `replay` on. The crash cascades past the one designed discriminating case (the autoplay-stream test) to every case in the 'startGameWith: the input recorder' block that reaches a simulating, replay-recording frame: 4 in loop.test.ts fail (the count's denominator moves with the file -- 205 when this was re-measured, 245 at the controllers-1-4 PR; `expectFailures` pins the 4, not the denominator) ('records exactly one tick per simulated tick...', 'captures the AUTOPLAY stream...', 'stamps the world it is recording against...', 'produces a trace that replays the recorded run exactly'). The two cases in that same block that never reach such a frame ('records nothing while the game is not simulating', 'does not record at all with the flag off') still pass, so the killed outcome remains driven by input reaching the sim, exactly as before -- only the count and mechanism (a thrown error, not a silently-empty trace) moved. Re-verified through this harness (`npm run mutate -- --only replay-recorder-wraps-the-raw-controller`) at the commit that landed the list-shaped input change; the 1-failure figure predates that PR.
killedBy: startGameWith: the input recorder captures the AUTOPLAY stream, which is what wrapping effectiveInput buys
startGameWith: the input recorder produces a trace that replays the recorded run exactly
startGameWith: the input recorder records exactly one tick per simulated tick, and leaves sampling untouched
